newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Offers seen but buying interest low.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Offers seen but buying interest low.

text.p: Offers emerged in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Thursday but failed to attract buyers amid slack demand, traders said.
Offers for the 180-cst were heard at $102 and $102.50 per tonne but there was no buying interest, they said.
"The market is a little directionless today. People are searching for market-moving factors but there is none," said one trader.
The Singapore weekly residue stocks, which fell 465,000 barrels to 10.312 million barrels for the week ending June 4, had little impact on the market, traders said.

On Thursday, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought two 38,000-tonne 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil cargoes for July deliveries at $129 and $123 per tonne respectively on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
On the demand side, state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is seeking to buy 10,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade, 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for late June delivery on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
The tender, IOC's first purchase tender for June delivery, will close on June 12 and is valid for one day.
"India may need to buy more for the summer season, but not many people will be interested in a 10,000-tonne deal. It's too small," said one dealer.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, July contract slipped 50 cents to $100.00, with 50 100-tonne lots traded.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) has decided to award a tender for a 500,000-barrel cargo to South Korea's Ssangyong Corp at $17.55 per barrel on Monday, a KEPCO source said.
The price compared to KEPCO's last purchase levels at $17.70 and $18.25 per barrel.
"The award level is just too low. The minimum cost should be at least $15.85 per barrel," said one trader.
However, traders said the market has improved a little from last month when the price was just above $15.00 per barrel.
"Demand will definitely improve as the summer season nears," the trader said.
